predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Kingdom of Polonnaruwa', 'Fall of Polonnaruwa: 1220'. The kingdom-of-polonnaruwa dossier (sa-03) also names this state as a successor of 1236. The Dambadeniya country lay in the south-west (Maya Rata), outside the northern realm that dossier keeps to 1236.

land.text: the Dambadeniya-Yapahuwa country, which Cliopatria folds into its 'Ceylon' row from 1294

successors.note: Cliopatria splits one Sinhalese realm into two rows: 'Ceylon' (the island round a hole at Kurunegala) and this row for 1236-1293, then one 'Ceylon' shape from 1294. The Dambadeniya page runs the same dynasty to 1345 (Yapahuwa 1271-1283, Polonnaruwa 1302-1310, Kurunegala 1310-1345) before the capital moved to Gampola.

capitals.name: Dambadeniya
capitals.note: Infobox 'Dambadeniya (1226-1271)'; the first king to choose it was Vijayabahu III (no year); 'a Buddhist convention in 1226'. Coordinates approximate.

capitals.name: Yapahuwa
capitals.note: Infobox 'Yapahuwa (1271-1283)'; text 'transferred the capital to Yapahuwa in 1273'. The infobox gives no capital 1284-1301 and then 'Polonnaruwa (1302-1310)'; Yapahuwa is kept to the end of the Cliopatria row. Coordinates approximate.

correction.text: the Dambadeniya-Yapahuwa country round Kurunegala (Cliopatria 1236 outline, about 5,200 km2)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1220-1235: the infobox gives the kingdom's rulers 'reigned from 1220-1345' and the first, Vijayabahu III, 1220-1224, with 'Fall of Polonnaruwa: 1220'; the area is not given. The outline used is Cliopatria's 1236 shape; the Polonnaruwa page (not opened here) has Vijayabahu III establishing Dambadeniya in 1232, which the Dambadeniya page does not support ('The text does not support 1232 or 1236'). [Reviewer sa-04-a: verdict ok to adjust: a new keyframe with from, to and a correction]

5,219 km2 round Kurunegala, 1236-1284. No infobox area. Parakramabahu II 'was crowned as the second king of Dambadeniya after the incident in 1236' (reign 1236-1270 on his page; 1234-1269 on the Dambadeniya infobox), 'successfully pushed Kalinga Magha out of Polonnaruwa by 1244' and 'annexed large parts of the North'; the rest of his realm is drawn by Cliopatria's 'Ceylon' row (ceylon dossier), so this small shape is the royal core, not the whole kingdom.

Same 5,219 km2 outline for 1285-1293: Yapahuwa (capital 1271-1283) lies inside it. The Pandyas 'captured the Tooth Relic, and carried it to India' in 1284; 'Bhuvanekabahu I' ruled 1272-1284 (infobox 1271-1283). Cliopatria ends the row in 1293 and folds the country into its Ceylon row; the Dambadeniya page keeps the dynasty to 1345.

region.text: the Dambadeniya-Yapahuwa country round Kurunegala (Cliopatria 1236 outline, about 5,200 km2)

ledger.note: 1220: the Sinhalese kingdom of Dambadeniya rises after the fall of Polonnaruwa. Infobox 'Fall of Polonnaruwa: 1220', first ruler Vijayabahu III (1220-1224) who 'was the first king to choose Dambadeniya as his capital' (no year); 'a Buddhist convention in 1226'.
1271: the court moves to Yapahuwa. Infobox 'Yapahuwa (1271-1283)'; text: 'Considering Dambadeniya insecure, he transferred the capital to Yapahuwa in 1273'; Bhuvanekabahu I (1272-1284).

region.text: the Yapahuwa country, where the Tooth Relic was kept

ledger.note: 1284: the Pandyas take the Tooth Relic. 'Pandyas of South India invaded, captured the Tooth Relic, and carried it to India' (1284); the Pandya Empire page adds that Kulasekara 'invaded Sri Lanka and carried away the Tooth Relic. Pandya control of Sri Lanka lasted until c. 1308-1309'. The region is my reading: the royal core where the relic was kept.

1293: the Cliopatria row ends with the occupation still running (the Pandya page ends Pandya control c. 1308-1309; the ceylon dossier carries the end). The Dambadeniya page has Parakramabahu III recover the relic in the passage dated 1287-1293.

1293: Cliopatria folds the Dambadeniya country into its Ceylon row. The Dambadeniya page does not end the kingdom: its infobox runs the line to 1345 (Yapahuwa, Polonnaruwa 1302-1310, Kurunegala 1310-1345), 'Succeeded by the Kingdom of Gampola, Capital moved to Gampola: 1345'; the page's own dates for 1287-1310 conflict (Parakramabahu III 1302-1310 on the infobox, 1287-1293 in the text).

wars.name: War of Parakramabahu II with Kalinga Magha
wars.outcome: Parakramabahu II 'successfully pushed Kalinga Magha out of Polonnaruwa by 1244'; Magha withdrew to Jaffna.
wars.note: The year the page gives is a bound ('by 1244'); the Polonnaruwa dossier dates Magha's expulsion 1236.

wars.name: Chandrabhanu's invasion of Dambadeniya
wars.outcome: 'the first one occurred in 1244, led by Chandrabhanu of Tambralinga'; repulsed; Chandrabhanu settled in the north (Jaffna) and later 'launched an invasion to the South' (undated).

wars.name: Pandya invasions of Sri Lanka
wars.outcome: 'a huge Pandyan invasion, launched by Sadayavarman Sundara, occurred sometime between the years 1254 and 1256', Dambadeniya 'not much affected'; the Pandyas capture the Tooth Relic in 1284.
wars.note: The Dambadeniya page dates only the 1284 capture; the Pandya Empire page (opened for pandya-empire) gives 1258, 1262-1264 and 1270.

certainty.note: No frontier of any kind is on the pages; the 5,219 km2 outline is Cliopatria's.
